question: Which of the following Governor-Generals of British India was in favour of free press and repealed the press regulations of 1823?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Metcalfe**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Metcalfe** was the Governor-General of British India who was in favour of a free press.
 
• He is known for repealing the press regulations of 1823, which were imposed by John Adam, the acting Governor-General at the time.
 
• This act of repeal is considered a significant step towards the freedom of the press in India.
 
• Lord Metcalfe’s tenure as Governor-General was from 1835 to 1836.
 
• His efforts earned him the title of the "Liberator of the Indian Press."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The press regulations of 1823 were seen as repressive measures aimed at controlling the freedom of expression.
 
• These regulations required all newspapers to obtain a license from the government to publish.
 
• Lord Metcalfe's repeal of these regulations was a landmark event in the history of the Indian press, allowing for greater freedom of expression and the growth of journalism in India.
 
• His actions were praised by many contemporary Indian and British journalists and intellectuals.
